thread.title: SoftBank Puts Another $2B In Korean E-Commerce

author: VCDeals
title: SoftBank Puts Another $2B In Korean E-Commerce
text:
Welcome to Seeking Alpha’s Venture Capital Deals of the Week. Follow this account and turn on the e-mail alert to receive VCDeals in your inbox on Saturday mornings.
Korean e-commerce: SoftBank ( OTCPK:SFTBF , OTCPK:SFTBY ) Vision Fund invested $2B in Korean e-commerce startup Coupang, which would push valuation to $9B. Total funding now stands at $3.4B. The online retailer lists over 120M items in categories ranging from consumer electronics to food. Revenue is expected to reach nearly $5B by year’s end, more than doubling in two years. Coupang plans to go public sometime soon but not next year.
Lidar sensors: Intel (NASDAQ: INTC ) Capital was among the backers in a $40M Series B funding for Lidar technology developer AEye, which brings total funding to about $61M. Taiwan’s government-backed Taiwania Capital led as a strategic investor with participation from Kleiner Perkins, Airbus Ventures, and Tychee Partners. AEye claims it set a new record for the distance from which a lidar system can detect and track a moving object. AEye’s iDAR sensor could detect/track a truck from 1 km away, which the company says is up to 5x better than other lidar systems. The company thinks iDAR can eventually track from 5 km to 10 km away.
Competitors: Quanergy ($135M in total funding, Samsung among backers), Velodyne LiDAR ($150.2M in total funding, Baidu and Ford backing), and LeddarTech ($123M in total funding, Integrated Device backing).
European e-scooters : Berlin-based dockless e-scooter and electric bike startup Wind Mobility raised $22M in seed funding from Chinese Source Code Capital and Europe’s HV Holtzbrinck Ventures. Wind currently operates in various cities in Spain, France, Germany, and the United States. The company is developing its first proprietary model of scooter designed for bike sharing. The new funds will go toward global expansion and building out the e-scooter product.
Competitors: Uber ( UBER ) and Lyft ( LYFT ) have entered the bike-share space with the acquisition of Jump Bikes and Motivate, respectively. In Europe, Wind competes against Bird and Lime. Smaller startup competitors include Sweden’s VOI (recently raised $50M) and Germany’s Tier (recently raised €25M).
Bitmoji competitor: Snap (NYSE: SNAP ) Bitmoji competitor Genies raised $10M in a party round that included NEA, Tinder’s Sean Rad, athlete Carmelo Anthony, and musician A$AP Rocky. The Genies iOS and Android apps let the user chat through an avatar, which acts out keywords and the general sentiment of the message. The company is launching an SDK that charges other apps to let users create avatars to use in chat, games, animations, and AR.
Competitors: Facebook (NASDAQ: FB ) is working on an Avatars feature that was announced several months ago but hasn’t reached the public testing phase. Google’s (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) Gboard can create avatars based on a selfie, but they’re lower in detail than Genies. Apple’s (NASDAQ: AAPL ) Memoji looks more generic than Genies but has similar functionality.
Exit: Autodesk (NASDAQ: ADSK ) acquired construction productivity software company PlanGrid for $875M in cash. PlanGrid raised $66M in private funding.
